findings.sentence: **open-code-review** uses fixed rule steps for most of the work.
findings.reason: The evidence says only that the project combines deterministic engineering with an agent. It says nothing about how much of the work each part does, so 'most of the work' goes beyond the source.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Open Code Review's core philosophy is to combine deterministic engineering with an agent, each handling what it does best.
findings.suggested_correction: The project says it combines fixed, rule-based steps with an AI agent, each handling what it does best.

findings.sentence: An AI agent (a model that takes steps on its own) only makes the judgment calls.
findings.reason: The supplied text does not limit the agent to 'only' judgment calls or describe how work is split. The narrow role is an inference.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Open Code Review's core philosophy is to combine deterministic engineering with an agent, each handling what it does best.
findings.suggested_correction: An AI agent (a model that takes steps on its own) handles the parts the project says suit an agent best.

findings.sentence: That makes its output easier to explain to an auditor than a free-form AI review.

findings.sentence: It claims better precision than Claude Code at about one-ninth the tokens, but that is the project's own test.
findings.reason: The draft correctly credits the claim to the project, but no supplied excerpt contains the precision, Claude Code comparison, 1/9 token figure or AACR-Bench details. The specific numbers cannot be checked.

findings.sentence: The **HIPAA Privacy Rule** update lets health plans share patient data to coordinate care for one person, not just groups.
findings.reason: The evidence says the rule 'confirms' an existing permission. It does not say the permission is new, and it does not compare with a prior groups-only rule. Both 'lets' (as if newly allowed) and 'not just groups' add a before-and-after contrast the evidence does not contain.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Confirms that health plans may use and disclose PHI for care coordination and case management for specific individuals.
findings.suggested_correction: According to a K&L Gates summary, the HIPAA Privacy Rule update confirms that health plans may use and share patient data for care coordination and case management for specific individuals.

findings.sentence: Stricter state consent laws and Part 2 rules for addiction records still apply.
findings.reason: The supplied excerpts do not mention 42 CFR Part 2 or state consent laws.
findings.suggested_correction: Check with counsel whether 42 CFR Part 2 and stricter state consent laws still limit this sharing (not covered in the supplied evidence).

findings.sentence: Patients must get copies of their records in **15 days**, down from 30.
findings.reason: The evidence sets a deadline for 'acting on a request', not a guarantee that patients receive copies. It also does not rule out an extension; the draft's own Items section mentions a 30-day extension. The sentence states a firmer, wider duty than the evidence supports.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Cuts the deadline for acting on a request for copies of PHI from 30 to 15 calendar days.
findings.suggested_correction: Per a K&L Gates summary, the deadline for acting on a patient's request for copies of their records drops from 30 to 15 calendar days (an extension may apply).

findings.sentence: You have until **17 July 2027** to comply.
findings.reason: No supplied excerpt gives a compliance date, effective date or Federal Register publication date. The draft itself says the Federal Register text was not read.
findings.suggested_correction: A law-firm summary reportedly gives a compliance date of 17 July 2027 (not in the supplied evidence). Confirm it in the Federal Register before planning around it.

findings.sentence: First, the **HIPAA** rule has a firm compliance date of **17 July 2027**.
findings.reason: The compliance date is not in the supplied evidence. 'Firm' overstates certainty for a date taken from a secondary law-firm summary and not checked against the Federal Register. The sentence also does not separate the compliance date from the effective date or the publication date.
findings.suggested_correction: First, a law-firm summary reports a HIPAA compliance date of 17 July 2027 (separate from the effective date). Confirm it in the Federal Register text.

findings.sentence: Budget now for faster records requests, new fee notices and updated vendor contracts (business associate agreements).

findings.suggested_correction: Suggestion: budget for faster records requests and advance fee notices, and ask counsel whether vendor contracts (business associate agreements) need changes.
